title: trust
content:
Trust runs everything. That's the thing I can't stop thinking about.
Laws? Trust, dressed up in paperwork. Probabilities? A bet you're placing on trust, whether you know it or not. Zoom out far enough and it almost feels like intelligence itself is just trust, distributed.

We built our whole world on top of it. Economies. Technology. Relationships. Take trust out of any of these and watch them collapse in real time.

But here's the one nobody talks about: does your own body trust you?
Say you're going to do something. Feel that? That's not just words leaving your mouth, that's a force behind them, or the absence of one. Your body already knows the difference between "yeah sure, whatever" and "let's actually go." 

It's been keeping score the whole time. Omg, this guy always talks, never delivers. Or: heyy, finally, let's see what we've got.

The body wants to trust you. It's rooting for you, every incentive lined up in your favor. But break that pattern enough times, say one thing and do another, and it pulls back. Quietly. It brings in other mechanisms. Resistance. Drag. Static. A built in defense system against your own nonsense. Honestly? Miraculous engineering.

Now here's the flip side, the good part. Stay with your body. Actually present, actually there, not just occupying space while your mind runs somewhere else. And something shifts. The same boring task stops being boring. It feels new. Almost like you're doing it for the first time, every time. Resistance just... goes. That's not motivation. That's trust, rebuilt.

But don't get comfortable. The moment you think "okay, I've earned it, I can coast now," the body clocks it instantly. It doesn't do participation trophies. Slack off and the resistance comes right back, no warning shot.

That's the whole game. Trust isn't a status you unlock and keep. It's a live wire. Always moving, always being tested, never fully settled.
Maybe that's the one thing you actually can trust: nothing stays trustworthy on its own. It has to be earned again. Every time.
